name: Least-privilege RBAC and token hardening
objective: CKS › Cluster + System Hardening (15% + 15%). Drill EVERY hardening corner harder than the exam on a real multi-node kind cluster: control-plane manifest perms, kubelet read-only port + anonymous-auth + authz mode, two apiserver admission/flag hardenings, least-privilege RBAC, ServiceAccount token hardening, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Least-privilege RBAC for a workload
questions.teach:
Give a workload the minimum API access: a narrow namespaced **Role** (only the verbs/resources needed) bound to its ServiceAccount via a **RoleBinding** — never `cluster-admin`. Imperatively: `kubectl create role r --verb=get,list --resource=pods` then `kubectl create rolebinding rb --role=r --serviceaccount=<ns>:<name>`.

**Gotcha:** `--serviceaccount` takes `ns:name`, not just the name.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-learn` a ServiceAccount `reader` already exists. Create a Role granting only `get,list` on `pods` and a RoleBinding binding it to that SA.

Target: SA `reader` can `list pods` (`yes`) but cannot `delete pods` (`no`) in `cks-learn`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-learn create role pod-reader --verb=get,list --resource=pods`, then `kubectl -n cks-learn create rolebinding reader-pr --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=cks-learn:reader`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n cks-learn create role pod-reader --verb=get,list --resource=pods
kubectl -n cks-learn create rolebinding reader-pr --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=cks-learn:reader
kubectl auth can-i list pods   --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:reader -n cks-learn   # yes
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:reader -n cks-learn   # no

verification.description: SA reader can list pods but cannot delete pods in cks-learn

questions.title: ServiceAccount token hardening
questions.teach:
By default every pod auto-mounts a ServiceAccount token an attacker could steal. For pods that never call the API, set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the **ServiceAccount**, then point the pod at it with `serviceAccountName` so it gets no token volume.

**Gotcha:** `automountServiceAccountToken` sits at the **top level** of the SA object, not inside a `spec:` block — a common YAML mistake.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-learn`, create a ServiceAccount `no-token` with `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, then run a pod `hardened` (image `busybox:1.36`, e.g. `sleep 3600`) using that ServiceAccount.

Target: SA `no-token` has `automountServiceAccountToken: false` AND pod `hardened` runs as SA `no-token` with no SA token volume mounted.
questions.hint: Create the SA with `automountServiceAccountToken: false` (top level), then create the pod with `serviceAccountName: no-token`. Apply with `kubectl apply -f -`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: no-token
  namespace: cks-learn
automountServiceAccountToken: false
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hardened
  namespace: cks-learn
spec:
  serviceAccountName: no-token
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
YAML

verification.description: SA no-token has automount disabled and pod hardened uses it with no token mounted
